summary: Approve at 3d0e798. The fix_task is closed on verified evidence: both sides of the ceiling's justification now point the same way and the arithmetic checks out. No blocking findings remain.
notes: SCOPE: this artifact records three passes - the full review of 13c5a31, the scoped delta review of ae0ccd6, and this final verification of the correction 3d0e798. Findings are marked CLOSED or CARRIED FORWARD accordingly.

CLOSED - fix_task corregir-direccion-del-margen-en-adr-0030. The corrected sentence is unambiguous AND correct, not merely different. Each comparison now names its subject explicitly ('el techo queda muy por encima de...' twice) instead of relying on an implied plural, and both sides point the same way. Verified: zero occurrences of 'por debajo de la secuencia' anywhere under docs/ or crates/. The imprecise 'un orden de magnitud' framing that carried the error is gone from the ADR, replaced by two exact figures.

CLOSED - arithmetic checked rather than assumed. 1000 / 0.047 = 21277, so 'unas 21.000 veces' is right; log10 of that ratio is 4.33, so 'cuatro ordenes de magnitud' is correct as a rounded-down floor. 1000 / 140 = 7.14, so 'mas de siete veces lo que tarda la promocion completa' is exact and, better, conservative: it takes the SLOWEST end of the 88-140 ms promotion range, which yields the smallest multiple and therefore the weakest and safest form of the claim. The detection argument is sound as stated.

Adding the argument to D-37 was the right call, judged on independent grounds rather than by deferring to the implementer. Three reasons. (a) The repo makes both records append-only - ADRs are superseded by a new ADR and never rewritten, bitacora entries are never edited or deleted - so two immutable copies cannot silently drift; the only divergence path is adr-0030 being superseded later, and a stale trail entry is precisely what a register that 'decides nothing, it leaves a trail' exists to hold. (b) The single-copy failure is not hypothetical here: it ALREADY materialised in this task, where the detection argument lived only in adr-0030, was recorded backwards there, and D-37 carried nothing to cross-check it against. (c) It is not gratuitous duplication but a genuine gap in D-37's own rationale: 'the ceiling is not blind' is part of why discarding the strict wall was acceptable, so the discard's reasoning was incomplete without it. One rule-adjacent point checked and cleared: amending D-37 is not the forbidden editing of an existing entry, because D-37 was itself created in ae0ccd6 on this same unmerged branch and is still being authored; the rule protects the merged historical record, and the coordinator confirmed no renumbering.

The correction introduced nothing. It is docs-only, the tests class numstat is identical to the previous commit, docs moved 167 to 175 against a cap of 200, discard numbering D-34 through D-37 is intact, and the new paragraph contradicts nothing in the code, D-37, STATUS.md or AC-5.

LOW, explicitly NOT blocking and NOT a fix_task, recorded only so it is not mistaken for an oversight: estres_conmutacion.rs:105 still describes the ceiling as 'un orden de magnitud por encima' of the full promotion sequence, where the true ratio is 7.1x, about 0.85 orders. It is a colloquial round-up, not a contradiction - the direction now matches everywhere and the same 1000 vs 88-140 ms figures are cited in all three places, with the ADR and D-37 stating the multiple exactly. It predates this correction (it arrived with ae0ccd6) and the correction narrowed the gap rather than widening it, and at 7x above the entire promotion sequence the detection argument holds whichever phrasing is used.

CARRIED FORWARD, CLOSED - the medium NFR-03 finding from the first review. The flake mechanism I identified (a single ~10 ms preemption of the promoting thread, which must win a blocking con_lectura mutex against 20 saturating readers, breaking a 10 ms wall on a 2-core runner) no longer has a wall at that scale. Verified independently: zero residual 10.0 in the stress test, and crates/hexcell-storage/tests/promocion.rs:377 still asserts duracion_de_conmutacion_ms < 10.0 in a file that grep confirms spawns no threads and uses no Barrier, so NFR-03 keeps its strict certification under the uncontended condition the requirement actually describes. Coverage was not lost, only the duplicate wall under artificial contention.

CARRIED FORWARD - the relaxed ceiling is a real guard, not decorative. Its evidence targets the exact mechanism I flagged (12 of 44 runs pinned to two cores with external load), and the threshold is meaningful rather than merely unreachable because it sits above the ENTIRE promotion sequence: exceeding it means the pointer swap outlasted the whole operation it is a fraction of, which is a change of class from computing to waiting, not a latency regression.

CARRIED FORWARD - contract-check ok=true, violations none; not_checked: forbid.behaviors, covered by hand: crates/hexcell-storage/src/** untouched, no manifest or Cargo.lock change, no dev-dependencies, no tokio/async/.await, no std::env::set_var or remove_var, D-33 not routed around, adr-0028 grep guard step in ci.yml intact.

CARRIED FORWARD - AC-1..AC-8 all genuinely asserted, not merely arranged. AC-1 twice and disjointly (effective width, and live SQLite connections on the epoch inode). AC-2 by requiring both epoch markers plus zero impure and zero empty reads. AC-3 by zero contentions AND zero failures of any kind. AC-4 by -wal/-shm non-existence after drain and purge. AC-6 by strict FD equality. AC-7 by #[ignore] plus the named CI step. AC-8 by the promoted comun::preparar_staging_valido. AC-5 as rewritten is satisfied by reporting both durations and asserting only the ceiling.
CARRIED FORWARD - LOW: reader-thread errors are counted into fallos_de_lectura but the ErrorDeAlmacen is dropped, so if AC-3 ever fires in CI the operator gets a count with no error text.

CARRIED FORWARD - LOW: the wide-span check (is_finite() && >= 0.0 on an Instant::elapsed() value) is tautological; AC-5 requires only that the span be measured and reported distinctly, so it satisfies the criterion but is a report, not a guard.

CARRIED FORWARD - flakiness review found no hang or deadlock, and the file-descriptor workaround is sound rather than concealing a leak in src/**: the parked descriptor is SQLite unix-VFS per-inode deferred-close behaviour, bounded at one per inode and released when the inode's last connection closes.

CARRIED FORWARD, ESCALATED SEPARATELY BY THE ORCHESTRATOR - nothing mechanically protects the strict assertion at tests/promocion.rs:377 on which this entire relaxation depends, while D-37 names its deletion as a reopening trigger and this repo already institutionalised exactly that argument with the adr-0028 grep guard. Out of scope for AC-5 and deliberately not affecting this verdict.

CARRIED FORWARD - documentary rules satisfied: adr-0030 correlative and highest, README row present, STATUS.md dated 2026-09-07, D-35/D-36/D-37 with reasons and reopening conditions, no renumbering or deletion of existing entries. Spanish and didactic-comment standard met throughout.
